title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 23
statement:
Tom has twelve slips of paper which he wants to put into five cups labeled \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E.\)

He wants the sum of the numbers on the slips in each cup to be an integer. Furthermore, he wants the five integers to be consecutive and increasing from \(A\) to \(E.\) The numbers on the papers are \(2,\) \(2,\) \(2,\) \(2.5,\) \(2.5,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(3.5,\) \(4,\) \(4.5.\) If a slip with \(2\) goes into cup \(E\) and a slip with \(3\) goes into cup \(B,\) then the slip with \(3.5\) must go into what cup?

solutions.text:
The sum of all the slips is \(35,\) so the five consecutive integer cup sums must average \(7.\) Therefore cups \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) and \(E\) must have sums \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(8,\) and \(9,\) respectively.

Cup \(B\) already contains a \(3\) and must sum to \(6,\) so it must contain another \(3.\) Cup \(E\) already contains a \(2,\) so the other slips in \(E\) must sum to \(7.\)

The \(3.5\) slip cannot go in \(A,\) because cup \(A\) would need another \(1.5.\) It cannot go in \(B,\) which is already full. It cannot go in \(C\) or \(E,\) because either would then need another \(3.5,\) and no remaining slips can make that total. Cup \(D\) works, for example with \(3.5+4.5=8.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The five cup sums must be consecutive integers with total \(35.\)
After filling cup \(B,\) test where the \(3.5\) slip can still leave possible sums.
